title: When Communication Feels Difficult
subtitle: 在难以沟通的时刻，用更准确的英语理解情绪、边界与冲突。

items.meaning: 情绪容量；处理情绪或压力的精力
items.example: I don’t have the emotional bandwidth for a serious talk tonight.

items.meaning: 设定界限；明确自己能接受和不能接受的事
items.example: Setting boundaries can protect a healthy relationship.

items.meaning: 认可某人的感受或经历是合理、真实的
items.example: You can validate her feelings without agreeing with her decision.

items.meaning: 误解；错误理解某人的话或意图
items.example: He misinterpreted my silence as anger.

items.meaning: 潜在问题；表面冲突背后的真正原因
items.example: The missed call was not the underlying issue.

items.meaning: 相互的；双方都有付出或回应的
items.example: Trust grows when respect is reciprocal.

items.meaning: 缓和；降低冲突或紧张局势的强度
items.example: A calm question can help de-escalate an argument.

sections.label: Reading
sections.title: 英语短文
sections.heading: When Communication Feels Difficult
paragraphs: Communication often becomes difficult not because people do not care, but because they are tired, defensive, or afraid of being misunderstood. A short reply may be misinterpreted as coldness, while silence may look like rejection. Before reacting, it helps to ask what the other person meant rather than assuming the worst.

When someone is upset, trying to solve the problem immediately is not always helpful. First, validate the feeling: “I can see why that hurt you.” Validation does not mean that you agree with every conclusion. It simply shows that you are listening and that the other person’s experience matters.

Healthy communication also requires boundaries. If you lack the emotional bandwidth to continue, you can say, “I want to discuss this, but I need twenty minutes to calm down.” Respecting that boundary gives both people space to think. A pause should not be used as punishment; it should be a clear, respectful step toward returning to the conversation.

Finally, focus on the underlying issue and use language that de-escalates the conflict. Instead of blaming—“You never listen”—try describing your experience: “I felt ignored when I was interrupted.” Good communication is reciprocal: both people listen, clarify, and take responsibility. The goal is not to win, but to understand each other well enough to move forward.

items.pattern: It is not that A, but that B.
items.explanation: 不是因为 A，而是因为 B。用于纠正常见误解，并指出更准确的原因。A、B 后通常接完整从句。
items.example: It is not that she does not care, but that she needs time to process her feelings.

items.explanation: 与其做……，不如试着做……。instead of 和 try 后都使用动名词，适合提出温和、具体的替代方案。
items.example: Instead of assuming the worst, try asking a calm question.

items.question: A calm tone can help ______ an argument before it becomes worse.
用 Instead of + doing..., try + doing... 改写：Do not blame the other person. Ask what they meant.
According to the passage, why is validating someone’s feelings different from agreeing with every conclusion?

sections.label: Check Your Work
sections.title: 答案
items: Instead of blaming the other person, try asking what they meant.
Because validation recognizes that the other person’s feelings and experience are real and matter; it does not mean accepting every interpretation or decision as correct.
